title: Particles, isotopes and relative atomic mass; The mole and Avogadro constant; Mass spectrometry of elements; Mass spectrometry and IR of molecules
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM01#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM01#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS01#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS01#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM01#N.3a, AN01#N.3, AS01#N.5a, AS02#N.6a, AM01#N.5a, AN01#N.4, AS01#N.7a, AS02#N.8, AM01#N.8a, AN01#N.6, AS01#N.15, AS02#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amount of substance
items.clue: The quantity with symbol n, found by dividing a mass by M.

items.label: Avogadro constant
items.clue: Multiply n by this value to get the number of particles, N.

items.label: Mass number
items.clue: The total count of protons and neutrons in a nucleus, symbol A.

items.label: Atomic number
items.clue: The count of protons in a nucleus, symbol Z, which fixes the element.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in 0.500 mol of water, H₂O? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
Which statement about the molecular ion peak in the mass spectrum of an organic compound is correct?

options.text: It is the tallest peak, as most molecules reach the detector unbroken.
It is due to an ion formed when a molecule gains an electron.
Any peak at lower m/z than it shows an impurity in the sample.
Its m/z value gives the relative molecular mass of the compound.

questions.explanation: M⁺ is the whole molecule minus one electron. With a charge of 1+, its m/z equals Mr.

questions.stem: An ion X³⁺ contains 23 electrons and 30 neutrons. Which nuclear symbol represents this ion? (Each symbol is written with its superscript first and its subscript second.)
questions.explanation: Protons = 23 + 3 = 26 = Z. Mass number = 26 + 30 = 56. (X is iron.)

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of element E shows three peaks from singly charged atomic ions: m/z 24 (relative abundance 100), m/z 25 (relative abundance 12.7) and m/z 26 (relative abundance 13.9). What is the relative atomic mass of E, calculated from these data?
A student writes: 'Mr of carbon dioxide, CO₂ = 44.0 g mol⁻¹'. Which comment on this statement is correct?

options.text: It is correct: Mr and molar mass are one and the same quantity.
The unit is wrong: Mr is the mass of one molecule in grams.
The unit is wrong: Mr is measured in atomic mass units.
The unit is wrong: Mr is a ratio of masses, with no unit.

questions.explanation: Mr compares a CO₂ molecule with 1/12 of a carbon-12 atom; units cancel. M(CO₂) = 44.0 g mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: Methyl butanoate, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₃ (Mr = 102), gives a peak at m/z 71. Which neutral fragment was lost to form this ion?
questions.explanation: 102 − 71 = 31: OCH₃. Losing the methoxy group leaves CH₃CH₂CH₂CO⁺ (m/z 71), a sign of a methyl ester.

questions.stem: Chlorine (atomic number 17) has isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37. Pure samples of ³⁵Cl₂ gas and ³⁷Cl₂ gas are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The ³⁷Cl₂ gas diffuses more slowly than ³⁵Cl₂.
The two gases diffuse at the same rate as each other.
The two gases undergo different chemical reactions.
The ³⁷Cl₂ molecules contain more electrons than ³⁵Cl₂.

questions.explanation: At the same temperature the heavier ³⁷Cl₂ molecules move more slowly on average. Diffusion rate is a physical property.

questions.stem: Bromine atoms are about 50% ⁷⁹Br and 50% ⁸¹Br. Which describes the Br₂⁺ molecular-ion peaks in the mass spectrum of bromine?

options.text: m/z 158 and 162 only, in the ratio 1 : 1

questions.explanation: ½ × ½ = ¼ for 158 and for 162; 2 × ½ × ½ = ½ for 160. Ratio 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: How many ions are there in 5.55 g of calcium chloride, CaCl₂? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; Ar: Cl 35.5, Ca 40.1)
A compound gives a molecular ion at m/z = 58.0417 in a high-resolution mass spectrum. Use ¹H 1.0078, ¹²C 12.0000, ¹⁴N 14.0031, ¹⁶O 15.9949. What is its molecular formula?
Bromine's relative atomic mass is 79.90, almost exactly halfway between 79 and 81. What does this show?

options.text: Most bromine atoms are bromine-80, with 45 neutrons each.
Every bromine atom has the same mass, 79.90, between those of its two isotopes.
Bromine is a mixture of bromine-79 and bromine-81 atoms in roughly equal numbers.
Bromine's electrons add 0.90 to the mass of each bromine-79 atom.

questions.explanation: 50.7% ⁷⁹Br and 49.3% ⁸¹Br weight the two masses almost equally: (78.918 × 50.69 + 80.916 × 49.31) ÷ 100 = 79.90.

questions.stem: The electron-impact mass spectrum of a liquid has peaks at m/z 15, 29, 31, 45 and 46, plus a very small peak at 47. Which compound could it be? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0)
questions.explanation: Mᵣ = 2(12.0) + 6(1.0) + 16.0 = 46.0, matching M⁺ at 46. The tiny 47 peak is M+1.
